newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-CAPRIATI'S ERRORS COST HER DEAR AGAINST SANCHEZ VICARIO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI'S ERRORS COST HER DEAR AGAINST SANCHEZ VICARIO.

text.p: Jennifer Capriati managed only sporadic resistance as she lost in straight sets to world number two Arantxa Sanchez Vicario in the second round of the $450,000 Filderstadt tournament on Wednesday.

Capriati, playing her first event since the U.S. Open in August, produced plenty of her trademark booming forehands but also a large number of unforced errors in going down 6-4 6-4 in the second round tie.

The American, who has returned to the circuit part-time this year after a two-year break during which she battled against personal problems, scored a surprise straight sets win over Natalia Zvereva of Belarus in the first round.
But against the Spanish world number two, she only briefly looked like averting the inevitable, when she held three break points at 4-5 down with Sanchez serving for the match.
Sanchez fought her way back to deuce with the help of an ace, which was ruled in by the umpire after the line-judge had called it out, and an unforced groundstroke error by Capriati.
Sanchez clinched the match on her first match point by pressuring Capriati into overhitting a volley.
Nevertheless, the 20-year-old 1992 Olympic champion, wearing a support bandage to protect an elbow injury which has troubled her for over three years, felt her comeback was on track.
"I feel like I'm in better shape than I have ever been," said Capriati. "I played pretty good, I'm pleased with my game, I just have to keep working at it."
